processes.title: Invoice Increase Request
processes.memory_hook: The invoice was too low; calculate the delta and bill only the correction.
processes.business_intent: Increase the price or quantity value of an existing invoice through a controlled request that calculates the delta and later creates a debit memo.

control_plane.why: provides the original billed quantity and value
defines the new target amount and therefore the delta
controls when the correction can become a debit memo

data_hinges.changes: reference value and copied commercial context
financial correctness of the resulting debit memo

impact_summary: The process changes billed value and receivables without changing physical delivery; SAP calculates the difference between original and corrected values.
constraints: Use this when an existing invoice needs an increase, not when a new unrelated charge should be raised.
Reference and pricing-date rules matter because the process corrects a historical commercial event.
lead_questions: Why is invoice increase preferable to a generic debit memo request here?
Which values are copied from the invoice and which are corrected?
What approval or billing block protects the customer from an accidental increase?

processes.title: Preliminary Billing
processes.memory_hook: Agree on the invoice before the invoice becomes accounting truth.
processes.business_intent: Create a non-posting preliminary billing document for customer negotiation or internal approval before creating the final billing document.

control_plane.why: decide which billable references enter the preliminary stage
controls whether the preliminary document is ready to become final
transfers the agreed billing content into a posting-relevant document

data_hinges.changes: what customer is asked to approve
which commercial event is ultimately billed

impact_summary: The preliminary document is relevant for output and negotiation but not for posting to financial accounting; the final billing document remains the accounting event.
constraints: Preliminary billing is an optional intermediary, not a substitute for the legal/final billing document.
SAP does not support preliminary credit memos in the standard creation flow described for preliminary billing documents.
lead_questions: What business risk justifies a preliminary invoice stage?
Who may change the preliminary document and who approves it?
Which fields must remain identical when the final invoice is created?

processes.title: Retroactive Billing
processes.memory_hook: The price changed after the invoice. Recalculate history and settle only the difference.
processes.business_intent: Re-evaluate existing billing documents after pricing conditions change and create credit or debit memos for the resulting differences.

control_plane.why: find historical billing documents affected by the price change
calculates the new effective value using changed conditions
posts only the difference rather than recreating the original invoice

data_hinges.changes: whether a document falls into the changed-price period

impact_summary: Commercial history is re-evaluated after invoicing; the original invoice remains part of history while delta credit/debit documents settle the new agreement.
constraints: The retroactive billing list must be generated deliberately; changing a condition record does not itself automatically settle historical invoices.
Retroactive billing creates credit/debit memos with reference to billing documents, not sales documents.
Advanced Down Payment Processing cannot be combined with retroactive billing.
lead_questions: Which invoices are legally/commercially covered by the new price agreement?
How do returns and previous corrections affect the retroactive base?
How do we prevent repeated or duplicate adjustment?

processes.title: Billing Cancellation
processes.memory_hook: Do not edit accounting history into correctness. Reverse it, reopen the reference, then bill correctly.
processes.business_intent: Cancel an incorrect billing document by creating a cancellation document that nullifies the billing result and reopens the billed reference for correct billing where applicable.

control_plane.control: billing type and cancellation billing type
control_plane.why: define the document pair used for reversal
control accounting period and audit context
decides whether an offsetting FI entry must be posted

impact_summary: Cancellation creates a separate cancellation billing document; if the original was posted to FI, the cancellation must offset the accounting entry. The billed reference can become open for billing again.
constraints: Cancellation is not the same as a credit memo granted for a valid invoice; it says the billing document itself should be nullified.
Period locks, accounting status and downstream interfaces can constrain when cancellation is possible.
lead_questions: Was the invoice commercially valid but later credited, or was it simply wrong and should be canceled?
Which accounting period should carry the reversal?
What downstream tax/output/integration artifacts also need correction?

processes.title: Customer Down Payment with Milestone Billing
processes.memory_hook: The customer pays before final delivery, but the commercial schedule still lives in the sales document.

sap_scope_items.label: Sales Order Processing with Customer Down Payment

processes.deployment_scope: SAP S/4HANA and SAP S/4HANA Cloud variants where the classic milestone-billing down-payment process is available. Compare with Advanced Down Payment Processing before designing a new solution.
processes.business_intent: Request and clear a customer down payment before final billing when the sales order or contract uses milestone billing to control payment timing.

control_plane.why: decide when the down-payment request and final billing become due
creates the request from the sales document instead of treating the payment as an unrelated FI event
connects the commercial request with cash received and settlement on the final invoice

data_hinges.changes: when and how much is requested before final billing
whether cash has actually been received and can later be cleared
the remaining receivable after down-payment settlement

impact_summary: Sales and FI share the lifecycle: Sales controls the requested milestones while FI records the real payment and clearing.
The classic BKJ path is functionally and technically different from Advanced Down Payment Processing.
constraints: Do not mix classic milestone-based down-payment processing with Advanced Down Payment Processing inside one business transaction.
For a new design, compare the classic process with the newer advanced model instead of selecting BKJ only because it is familiar.
lead_questions: Why is a down payment required, and which milestone makes it due?
Which object proves that the customer actually paid, not only that a request was issued?
Are we extending a classic process or designing a new one where Advanced Down Payment Processing is the better boundary?
How are cancellation, partial payment and final clearing handled?
